current_example.title: Example: Evaluating a Triple Integral by Converting to Spherical Polar Coordinates

q-161750.name: Question 1
q-161750.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161750.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\rho }^{5}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161750.html:
Question 1
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=2. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rx2x2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫02ρ5cos2⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫02π∫02π∫02ρ5sin2⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫02ρ5cos2⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫02ρ3sin⁡θsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫02ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=x2x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2⋅ρ=ρ3cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx2x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ3cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫02ρ5cos2⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
q-161750.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere

q-161743.name: Question 2
q-161743.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161743.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161743.html:
Question 2
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=4. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rxx2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫02ρ4cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫02ρ3cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫02π∫04ρ3sin⁡θsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫0π∫04ρ4cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫0π∫02ρ3sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=xx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ=ρ2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rxx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫02ρ4cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161755.name: Question 3
q-161755.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=\frac{1}{4}.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}xz({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161755.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\frac{1}{2}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \frac{1}{2},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=xz({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xz({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{\rho }^{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161755.html:
Question 3
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=14. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rxz(x2+y2+z2)dV

a
∫02π∫02π∫01/2ρ4cos2⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫01/2ρ6cos⁡θcos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫01/4ρ6sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫01/4ρ4sin2⁡θsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫02ρ6cos2⁡θsin⁡θsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 12 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤12,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=xz(x2+y2+z2):

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρcos⁡ϕ⋅ρ2=ρ4cos⁡θcos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rxz(x2+y2+z2)dV=∭Δρ4cos⁡θcos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫01/2ρ6cos⁡θcos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161758.name: Question 4
q-161758.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}x+y\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161758.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 1,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=x+y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}x+y\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161758.html:
Question 4
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=1. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rx+ydV

a
∫0π∫02π∫01ρ3sin2⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)dρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫01ρ3(sin2⁡ϕcos⁡θ+sin⁡θcos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫0π∫01ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)dρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫01ρ3(sin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫0π∫01ρ4sin3⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)dρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤1,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=x+y:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ=ρsin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx+ydV=∭Δρsin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫01ρ3sin2⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+sin⁡θ)dρdθdϕ.

q-161762.name: Question 5
q-161762.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=36.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161762.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $6$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 6,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =((\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2})\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{6}{\rho }^{5}{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161762.html:
Question 5
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=36. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x2+y2)x2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫036ρ3sin2⁡ϕ(cos⁡θ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫06ρ5sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫036ρ5sin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫02π∫02π∫06ρ3sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫06ρ5sin2⁡ϕcos2⁡θdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 6 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤6,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=(x2+y2)x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=((ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2)⋅ρ=ρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)⋅ρ=ρ3sin2⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R(x2+y2)x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ3sin2⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫06ρ5sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161774.name: Question 6
q-161774.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6$ for $x\le 0$ and $z\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161774.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $\sqrt{6}$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/02834e98afa14d5193e5d560f85457e73caee7f5938af5ac8b3fb607165aad53.png)

 
As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{6},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}{\rho }^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161774.html:
Question 6
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=6 for x≤0 and z≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rx2dV

a
 ∫π/2π∫π/2π∫06ρ4sin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫π/2π∫π/22π∫06ρ3cos3⁡θsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫π/2π∫π/23π/2∫06ρ3sin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫π/2π∫π/23π/2∫06ρ4cos2⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫π/22π∫π/2π∫06ρ4cos2⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 6 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤6,π2≤θ≤3π2,π2≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=x2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2=ρ2cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx2dV=∭Δρ2cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫π/2π∫π/23π/2∫06ρ4cos2⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161766.name: Question 7
q-161766.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\ge 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161766.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/d497c83f7eb77b0b0950f5a1c1f5d429574b2734743ef91bbdb57541f7f7d90f.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 3,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}}} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161766.html:
Question 7
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=9 for x≥0 and z≥0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV

a
 ∫0π∫−π/2π/2∫03ρ3cos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π/2∫−π/2π/2∫03ρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π/2∫0π∫03ρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫0π∫03ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π/2∫π/2π∫03ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤3,−π2≤θ≤π2,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=zx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡ϕρ2=cos⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δcos⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫−π/2π/2∫03ρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161773.name: Question 8
q-161773.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2$ for $x\le 0$ and $z\ge 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161773.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/c4d31af830ee7d166662e88b1a7ade0c817d2508b887c15db5838d25b9467fca.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={({\rho }^{2})}^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{4}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\rho }^{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161773.html:
Question 8
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=2 for x≤0 and z≥0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x2+y2+z2)2dV

a
 ∫0π/2∫π/23π/2∫02ρ6sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π∫π/2π∫02ρ6sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π∫π/2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π/2∫π/23π/2∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π/2∫π/2π∫02ρ6sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2,π2≤θ≤3π2,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=(x2+y2+z2)2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρ2)2=ρ4

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R(x2+y2+z2)2dV=∭Δρ4⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫π/23π/2∫02ρ6sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161768.name: Question 9
q-161768.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161768.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/540ae5200e5628d721a64b2ee5ad2b3f0e3f7c3192ccb1f90aeab71abc93f070.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\sqrt{{({\rho }^{2})}^{3}} \\  & ={\rho }^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161768.html:
Question 9
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=4 for x≥0 and z≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x2+y2+z2)3dV

a
 ∫π/2π∫−π/2π/2∫02ρ5sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫π/2π∫−π/2π/2∫02ρ5cos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫π/23π/2∫−π/20∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫π/23π/2∫−π/20∫02ρ5sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫π/2π∫−π/2π/2∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2,−π2≤θ≤π2,π2≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=(x2+y2+z2)3:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρ2)3=ρ3

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R(x2+y2+z2)3dV=∭Δρ3⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫π/2π∫−π/2π/2∫02ρ5sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161759.name: Question 10
q-161759.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=5$ for $y\ge 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161759.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $\sqrt{5}$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/9ca3a428d54a15b11c4c5bd95039df6a0b2d9f4363dba7034c51edb2b6f8fd27.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{5},\,0\le \theta \le \pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}} \\  & =\rho \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\rho \cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{5}}{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161759.html:
Question 10
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=5 for y≥0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rx2+y2+z2dV

a
 ∫0π∫π2π∫05ρ3cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π∫π2π∫05ρ3cos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫0π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫−π/2π/2∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫0π∫05ρ4cos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 5 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤5,0≤θ≤π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρ2=ρ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫0π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/54ff64195ccfadddfe2b3ca0bb9e193147fedae20d8dae6a53a5ecddc3c26f5d.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-16y$ for $x\le 0$ and $z\ge 0,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161921.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$  represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $8$ centered at $(0,-8,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-16y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-16y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-16\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/868214a1c2b30da5b16b7f0c307b369bdc9f2d2201ee0ad5a3f5da2a8bdc6f49.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\sqrt{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{-16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 8 centered at (0,−8,0).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=−16y in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=−16yρ2=−16ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ(ρ+16sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=−16sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤−16sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,π≤θ≤3π2,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

q-161922.name: Question 12
q-161922.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/cf44412afd6f2a8eaab468676b4f6a9828f5000eec287234f9834a41e6816d5a.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=20x$ for $z\le 0,$ shown above.
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161922.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$  represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $10$ centered at $(10,0,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=20x$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =20x \\ {\rho }^{2} & =20\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/165ed50d8f94f3b896f4d19647fb514f544221872a6df241a6ab6c3797bbd698.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=20x for z≤0, shown above.
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Ryx2+y2dV

a
 ∫π/2π∫−π/2π∫020cos⁡ϕρsin⁡θdρdθdϕ
b
∫π/2π∫−π/2π/2∫020cos⁡θsin⁡ϕρsin⁡θdρdθdϕ
c

d

e

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 10 centered at (10,0,0).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=20x in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=20xρ2=20ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕρ(ρ−20cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=20cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤20cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,−π2≤θ≤π2,π2≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=yx2+y2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)=sin⁡θρsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Ryx2+y2dV=∭Δsin⁡θρsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫π/2π∫−π/2π/2∫020cos⁡θsin⁡ϕρsin⁡θdρdθdϕ.

q-161861.name: Question 13
q-161861.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/759ebc78c794f433bba8c1f555bc68b2da52de62741711f13bd9c9156e3c485e.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-2x,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161861.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $1$ centered at $(-1,0,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-2x$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-2x \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/43e3c386086d30431405bb3fe2ca2835595641041dd7e098f9234cab8e7b225d.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=−2x, shown above. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R1x2+y2+z2dV

a
 ∫0π∫03π/2∫0−cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ1ρ2dρdθdϕ.
b
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫0−2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
c
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫02cos⁡θsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
d
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫0−2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ1ρ2dρdθdϕ.
e
 ∫0π∫π3π/2∫0−cos⁡θsin⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 1 centered at (−1,0,0).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=−2x in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=−2xρ2=−2ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕρ(ρ+2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=−2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤−2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,π2≤θ≤3π2,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=1x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=1ρ2

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R1x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δ1ρ2⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫π/23π/2∫0−2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161918.name: Question 14
q-161918.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/110e46158875a0aeb3b3aa898b886ee03b8c4cf945e9853a4962e839c5b1f0f6.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-10y,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161918.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $5$ centered at $(0,-5,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-10y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-10y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-10\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +10\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-10\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/8f2c3d4810b8364e17ad82a0d271d9affe2714938bd7cccbc69c6174e1f03ec4.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -10\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\rho }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\rho }\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-10\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=−10y, shown above. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫π2π∫0−10sin⁡θsin⁡ϕρsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫0−10sin⁡θsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕρdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫02π∫0−5cos⁡ϕρsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫π2π∫0−5cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫π2π∫0−5cos⁡θcos⁡ϕρdρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 5 centered at (0,−5,0).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=−10y in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=−10yρ2=−10ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ(ρ+10sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=−10sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤−10sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,π≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=zx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡ϕρ2=cos⁡ϕρ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δcos⁡ϕρ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫π2π∫0−10sin⁡θsin⁡ϕρsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-40089.name: Question 15
q-40089.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/2206a1bc02acb9ddccc5991a4c8d36c9e5d3255e72239e8f7e81908e10faab48.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=18y$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\ge 0,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}xy\,\text{d}V
$$
q-40089.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $3$ centered at $(0,3,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=18y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =18y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =18\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/578c7f81a0dae8339772dec9a9407fb380866e5dde5fdd18fee04feb6afe5749.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=xy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xy\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-40089.html:
Question 15
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=18y for x≥0 and z≥0, shown above. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭RxydV

a
∫0π/2∫0π/2∫018cos⁡θsin⁡ϕρ3cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π/2∫0π/2∫018sin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ4cos⁡θsin⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫0π/2∫09sin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ4cos⁡θsin⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫0π/2∫09sin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ3cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π/2∫0π/2∫018cos⁡θsin⁡ϕρ2cos⁡θsin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 3 centered at (0,3,0).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=18y in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=18yρ2=18ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ(ρ−18sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=18sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤18sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,0≤θ≤π2,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=xy:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=ρ2cos⁡θsin⁡θsin2⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭RxydV=∭Δρ2cos⁡θsin⁡θsin2⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫0π/2∫018sin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ4cos⁡θsin⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-40155.name: Question 16
q-40155.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1.$
q-40155.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 1,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{2}{{\rho }^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{2}{{\rho }^{2}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}2\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}d\rho  \\  & =2[-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot [\rho ]_{\rho =0}^{\rho =1} \\  & =-2(-1-1)\cdot (2\pi -0)\cdot (1-0) \\  & =8\pi \end{aligned}
$$

a
2π2

2π3
c
8π

12π

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤1,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=2x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=2ρ2

∭R2x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δ2ρ2⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫012sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=2∫0πsin⁡ϕdϕ⋅∫02πdθ⋅∫01dρ=2[−cos⁡ϕ]ϕ=0ϕ=π⋅[θ]θ=0θ=2π⋅[ρ]ρ=0ρ=1=−2(−1−1)⋅(2π−0)⋅(1−0)=8π

q-161787.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/61bd212879bc2f37dba7637bb3b126e33c5f7b0fbebd5a676874d9b3f6bc38da.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6y$ for $x\ge 0,$ shown above.
q-161787.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $3$ centered at $(0,3,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =6y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =6\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/f52fe1c2e73dcbe972d72d263a5a43f2c99dbd573395fbf6e3a3b78b46e1f461.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}[\rho ]_{\rho =0}^{\rho =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}(6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-0)\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\theta  \\  & =6[ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =6(\pi -0)\cdot (-0+1) \\  & =6\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 3 centered at (0,3,0).

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=1x2+y2:

q-161597.name: Question 18
q-161597.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/ce36be89987c16762ad2b2e21d38cf78ec565f0aada219c982da6ea5eb958c1c.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{3z}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2x$ for $z\ge 0,$ shown above.
q-161597.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $1$ centered at $(1,0,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2x$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =2x \\ {\rho }^{2} & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/31a18ebb9608ff60a4a5ecbcfa8defcb6a64337b126cb5859cb042f1019b1194.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{3z}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{3\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\sqrt{({\rho }^{2})^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{3z}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ[\rho ]_{\rho =0}^{\rho =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-0)\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & =2\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,d\theta  \\  & =2\cdot [-{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =2\cdot [{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =2\cdot (1-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18
?

Evaluate the triple integral ∭R3z(x2+y2+z2)3dV over the region R enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=2x for z≥0, shown above.

a
π
b
0
c
6π
d
4
e
2π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 1 centered at (1,0,0).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=2x in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=2xρ2=2ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕρ(ρ−2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,−π2≤θ≤π2,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=3z(x2+y2+z2)3:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=3ρcos⁡ϕ(ρ2)3=3cos⁡ϕρ2

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R3z(x2+y2+z2)3dV=∭Δ3cos⁡ϕρ2⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫−π/2π/2∫02cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ3cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫−π/2π/23cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ[ρ]ρ=0ρ=2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫−π/2π/23cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ(2cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ−0)dθdϕ=∫0π/2∫−π/2π/26cos⁡θcos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdθdϕ=2⋅∫0π/23cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdϕ⋅∫−π/2π/2cos⁡θdθ=2⋅[−sin3⁡ϕ]ϕ=0ϕ=π/2⋅[−sin⁡θ]θ=−π/2θ=π/2=2⋅[sin3⁡ϕ]ϕ=0ϕ=π/2⋅[sin⁡θ]θ=−π/2θ=π/2=2⋅(1−0)⋅(1−(−1))=4

q-161789.name: Question 19
q-161789.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/085e28508da725e445c410fedc08a1992dccc5e0a7b99b3248182f58ffae2c07.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4z,$ shown above.
q-161789.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $2$ centered at $(0,0,2).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4z$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =4z \\ {\rho }^{2} & =4\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/8a730a72fe9f3f69878ef647215e8ed05e913f23bf8e0fab01bad6271e860335.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\rho }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{\rho }\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ{[\frac{1}{2}{\rho }^{2}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & =8{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }d\theta  \\  & =8{[-\frac{1}{3}{cos}^{3}⁡ϕ]}_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi } \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}(0-1)\cdot (2\pi -0) \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{3}\end{aligned}

Question 19
?

Evaluate the triple integral ∭R1x2+y2+z2dV over the region R enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=4z, shown above.

a
4π
b
8π
c
16π3
d
12π
e
9π4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas: x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 2 centered at (0,0,2).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=4z in spherical polar coordinates: x2+y2+z2=4zρ2=4ρcos⁡ϕρ(ρ−4cos⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=4cos⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤4cos⁡ϕ,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=1x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=1ρ2=1ρ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain
∭R1x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δ1ρ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫02π∫04cos⁡ϕρsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫02πsin⁡ϕ[12ρ2]ρ=0ρ=4cos⁡ϕdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫02π8sin⁡ϕcos2⁡ϕdθdϕ=8∫0π/2sin⁡ϕcos2⁡ϕdϕ⋅∫02πdθ=8[−13cos3⁡ϕ]ϕ=0ϕ=π/2⋅[θ]θ=0θ=2π=−83(0−1)⋅(2π−0)=16π3

q-161777.name: Question 20
q-161777.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/90d5e9115d216f2a7f8fba49295a36b95cd932c4df7f8bace1b45e3542e9ae11.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{3}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\ge 0,$ shown above.
q-161777.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/ec2f6c67eee7f836cc71efec2b17c2276aa8a9d397c632b3c499a46a75f7b95c.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 1,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={({\rho }^{2})}^{3} \\  & ={\rho }^{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{3}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{6}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\rho }^{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}{\rho }^{8}\,d\rho  \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{9}{\rho }^{9}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =1} \\  & =-(0-1)\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-(-\frac{\pi }{2}))\cdot \frac{1}{9}(1-0) \\  & =1\cdot \pi \cdot \frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{9}\end{aligned}
$$

q-161777.html:
Question 20
?

Evaluate the triple integral ∭R(x2+y2+z2)3dV over the region R enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=1 for x≥0 and z≥0, shown above.

a
3π2
b
5π8
c
3π
d
π
e
π9
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas: x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤1,−π2≤θ≤π2,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=(x2+y2+z2)3: f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρ2)3=ρ6

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain
∭R(x2+y2+z2)3dV=∭Δρ6⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫−π/2π/2∫01ρ8sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2sin⁡ϕdϕ⋅∫−π/2π/2dθ⋅∫01ρ8dρ=[−cos⁡ϕ]ϕ=0ϕ=π/2⋅[θ]θ=−π/2θ=π/2⋅[19ρ9]ρ=0ρ=1=−(0−1)⋅(π2−(−π2))⋅19(1−0)=1⋅π⋅19=π9
